title: Design System: Catalogue of a Run

archivo.stack: "Archivo", "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif
archivo.role: Every word and figure. Omnibus-Type, SIL OFL; embedded as a variable latin WOFF2 (tools/portal_v3/fonts/Archivo-latin-wdth.woff2), weight 100-900, width 62-125%, font-display: block; user-approved 2026-10-12. Tabular lining figures (tnum, lnum) on body.

mono.stack: "Cascadia Mono", Consolas, "SF Mono", Menlo, ui-monospace, monospace
mono.role: Platform face, not embedded: HL7 v2 segments, the retention record and audit lines only.

rootScale.purpose: Chrome and entry sizes are rem off this root.

plateScale.purpose: The plate's own font size; every plate object is in em off it.

widthAxis.value: figure and cover title 125 / unit 112 / entry 100 / labels 88-94 / field lists 90 / log 76
widthAxis.purpose: Hierarchy by width as well as weight.

stockVars.value: body[data-comp=a|b|c] sets --tint (plate ground) and --deep (figure, plate number, header mark, current index rule, caption letter); data-comp=cover sets --tint to night; none keeps stone and ink
stockVars.purpose: One switch re-tints a view to the pressed comparandum's stock.

shadows.name: blade

shadows.value: 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.45), 0 .15em .4em rgba(0,0,0,.55); .18em #d3d8db ring round a #e9ecee pin

shadows.name: phone-foot
shadows.purpose: The sticky foot over the scrolling book at 860px and below.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Every entrance and the travelling markers.

motion.name: engine
motion.value: WAAPI anim() with fill: backwards (holds its first frame through its delay, lands on the page's own style); rAF tween() for counting figures; busy() until the last ends; land() finishes every animation and tween
motion.purpose: One motion engine; a second Space (or any new step) lands what is playing.

motion.name: page-turn
motion.value: 880ms in a 2400px perspective; up 440ms cubic-bezier(.45,.05,.85,.55) to edge-on, the face fading over its last 16%; down 440ms cubic-bezier(.15,.45,.3,1); a shade band travels across a 300% gradient; cast shadow 0-1-0 over 528ms; the page beneath shades to .32
motion.purpose: Between plates; forward the plate plays from 820ms and the entry from 150ms; back the plate plays from 170ms. No leaf below 860px or under reduced motion.

motion.name: plate-timelines
motion.value: PLAY[plate](delay, k, {right}); marks staggered within a budget, gap(n, total, most)
motion.purpose: Each plate's object set in the order the run made it.

motion.name: count-by
motion.value: the figure fades in (240ms) with the first mark and sums the marks to the last + 60ms; unit with the first mark, caption at the end + 80ms, comparanda values 70ms apart
motion.purpose: A figure is counted only by the marks that make it.

motion.name: roll
motion.value: 760ms, cubic in-out; the new tint washed in behind a 3px roller edge in --deep at .3; a ghost of the old object clipped ahead of it; the new object clipped behind it; plate height eases cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)

motion.name: re-ink-in-place
motion.value: plate 3: each changed field 360ms at ROLL x atRoll(its x position)
motion.purpose: The inventory re-inked as the roller passes it.

motion.name: refigure
motion.value: numeric: count old to new on the roll curve, old ink pinned until mid-roll; a word or a change of breach state: the old stands to mid-roll, the new set whole rising from 14% (460ms)
motion.purpose: A breach is never counted into.

motion.name: comparanda-band
motion.purpose: The pressed row's tint band travels from the old row.

motion.name: index-rule
motion.purpose: The 2px place-marker over the plate index.

motion.name: page-edges
motion.purpose: The leaf stacks re-measure after a turn.

motion.name: fan
motion.value: fade 360ms; blades rotate from 0deg together, 1250ms, cubic-bezier(.22, 1.12, .36, 1); labels fade at 55%

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: anim() returns null, tween() steps to 1, no leaf; CSS animation and transition none

motion.name: keys
motion.value: Space / PageDown next (again while playing lands it), Shift+Space / PageUp back, Left / Right plate, Up / Down comparandum, a b c, 1-9 and 0, J job, M model, T told (Shift reverses), Home the cover, End the index; #0 the cover, #3b deep links

narrative.northStar: The Printed Catalogue, Open on the Table
narrative.overview:
Portal version 3 treats the recorded run as a collection and catalogues it. Every view is the same spread of an open book lying on a linen table under a lamp: on the left page a plate, one real object the pipeline made (the field inventory, the job's request slip, the extract, the browser's page-load log, the declared manifest, the HL7 v2 messages as they left, the retention record, every recorded run, the audit chain), tipped in on its stock; on the right page its catalogue entry, a plate number, a title, one figure set monumental, the comparanda a / b / c, and a short label/value record. Ours, an AI model and the baseline are flipped in place on the same plate: a new stock is rolled across it and the object re-inks behind the roller. A frontispiece opens the book: the three stocks as a swatch fan on a night plate, beside the title and the contents. There are no lanes, no dots, no flows and no tiles.

The world is a museum catalogue printed on coloured stocks, and since the finish pass (2026-10-15) it is a physical one: warm grained paper, a gutter that curves into the spine, the leaves already turned stacked at the left fore-edge and those to come at the right, the plate tipped in with a hairline lift and the grain printed into its tint, the whole book casting a soft umber shadow onto the linen. Each comparandum has its own stock, ours viridian, the AI model ultramarine, the baseline ochre; plates that belong to no comparandum (the hospital, the request, the index) stay on stone grey. One red, reserved for a breach, overrides any stock. One face, Archivo, carries everything; its width axis does the work a second face would. The platform mono is used for the three objects that are machine records in their own right: HL7 segments, the retention record and the audit lines.

Motion is held to the finish level of Portal v2 and every move is a recorded fact being set. A leaf turns in 3D between plates; each plate then plays its own timeline (fields ink in in the order the run read them, the log prints a line a page load, a rule is drawn under each control) and the figure appears with the first mark and counts the marks; a second Space lands whatever is playing. Density is presentation density for a projected 1366x768 laptop: three frame rows, nothing scrolls at the laptop size, the figure readable from the back of the room, words held to labels; the presenter explains.
keyCharacteristics: An open book on a lamp-lit linen table: grained paper pages, a shaded gutter, page-edge stacks that say where you are, the plate tipped in on its stock.
Three stocks (viridian a, ultramarine b, ochre c) tint a comparandum's plate and ink its figure; stone grey for shared plates; red only for a breach.
A frontispiece on a lit night plate: the three grained stocks as a swatch fan turning on a drawn eyelet rivet, the title set wide and light, a two-column contents list.
One embedded face, Archivo (variable weight 100-900, width 62-125%); platform mono only for HL7, the retention record and the audit lines.
One figure per entry, wide and light at up to 7rem, counted in step with the marks that make it.
Hairline rules, square corners, no cards, no pills; shadows only where paper lies on paper or on the table, always soft and umber.
Motion is the run being set: a 3D page turn, per-plate timelines, the comparanda roll; a second Space lands it; reduced motion lands everything.

rules.name: The Colour Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Colour names whose plate it is (a comparandum's stock) or a breach (red), nothing else. No category hues, no decorative accent; chrome stays ink, greys and the warm neutrals of paper and linen.

rules.name: The One Stock Per Plate Rule
rules.body: A plate carries at most one stock: the pressed comparandum's. Shared plates stay stone. The tint is the plate's ground; the deep colour goes only on the figure and the small markers that point at the comparandum (plate number, header mark, travelling index rule, roller edge, caption letter, tab).

rules.name: The Ghost Is Absence Rule
rules.body: Ghost grey means "held by the hospital, not taken by this run" (or "same as run 1", or "not declared"). It never styles chrome, and a read value is never ghosted.

rules.name: The Umber Is Shade Rule
rules.body: Shade on this table is warm umber at low alpha, never black and never a solid fill. Only the night plate, a dark object on its own, takes black shadows.

rules.name: The Width Is The Material Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from Archivo's width and weight axes, never a second display face. Wide and light means "the figure" (and the cover title); condensed means "a list of many"; mono means "a machine wrote this".

rules.name: The 13px Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing read is set below 0.8125rem of a root that is never below 16px (13px). Plate type is in em off a plate size that is never below 1rem, so its smallest step (0.8125em) holds the same floor.

rules.name: The Paper On Paper Rule
rules.body: A shadow is cast only where one physical thing lies on another: the book on the table, a plate on the page, a leaf over the spread, a blade on the night plate, a key on the table. Type, rules and figures never cast one.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: There is one light, centre-top over the table (upper left on the night plate), and every shade, gutter and cast shadow agrees with it. Nothing glows.

dos: **Do** put one real object the run produced on each plate, computed by the project's code, and set its one fact as the figure.

**Do** flip comparanda in place on the same plate by rolling the new stock across it; never set a, b and c side by side (the cover's fan, one object holding the three stocks, is the only place they meet).
**Do** print a comparandum's plates on its own stock: viridian for ours, ultramarine for the AI model, ochre for the baseline; keep shared plates on stone.
**Do** let red override the stock, and only where a figure or value measures a breach; keep the red underline on out-of-purpose fields as the second channel.
**Do** make every move a recorded fact being set, in the order the run made it, and count the figure only by the marks that make it.
**Do** let a second Space land whatever is playing, and land every state whole under reduced motion.
**Do** keep shade warm umber at low alpha, from one lamp, and only where paper lies on paper or on the table.
**Do** tip the plate in at the size of its object with the page's paper as its margin; let only the log and the cover fill the page.
**Do** size plate objects in em off the plate's font size, and chrome in rem off the root clamp.
**Do** fit by giving way (line height, whole messages counted, the figure stepping down), never by cutting a record mid-line.
**Do** keep the file single and offline: Archivo embedded, SVG, CSS and inline SVG noise only.
donts: **Don't** add lanes, dots, flows, metro lines, KPI tiles, cards or pills; the night ground belongs to the cover plate alone.
**Don't** add a hue beyond the three stocks and the breach red, or use a stock for chrome, categories or decoration.
**Don't** colour a figure red because of who measured it; only because it measures a breach, and never count a figure into or out of a breach.
**Don't** cast a shadow from type, rules or figures, use black shadows off the night plate, or use a hard offset.
**Don't** mark the chosen comparandum with a side stripe; it is a full-width tint band that travels.
**Don't** animate anything that is not a recorded fact, or leave anything moving once a step has landed.
**Don't** use mono outside HL7 segments, the retention record and the audit lines.
**Don't** set anything read below 0.8125rem (13px at the floor of the root clamp).
**Don't** show a raw identifier, contact detail or quasi-identifier; record numbers and names are masked and the builder refuses to write if one appears.
**Don't** add explanatory prose to a spread; labels, figures and one caption line; the presenter explains.
